name: security-oidc-logout-lifecycle-review
intent: OIDC front/back-channel logout and local session termination
artifacts: Logout token validation, sid/sub mapping, client sessions, logout endpoint and post-logout redirect policy.
trace: Trace issuer/session identity from a logout message to exactly the intended local sessions. Inspect replay and whether a notification merely clears UI state.
experiment: Use two owned issuer sessions and local sessions; compare intended logout, wrong-issuer/session message and a harmless replay.
disproof: A changed login screen is not proof that a server session was revoked; global logout may be an intentional policy rather than overbroad binding.
repair: Validate logout issuer/context and revoke the correct sessions; retest retained unrelated sessions and intended termination.
branch_decisions: Back-channel logout validation and front-channel browser state are different paths. Resolve sid/sub and issuer/client binding before selecting sessions. Browser cookie restrictions may block front-channel effects; a local logout UI change is not evidence that a server session or refresh family ended.
operational_method: Validate a back-channel logout token as its own token class: signature/context, required logout event, issuer/audience, time and sid/sub selection; reject a Logout Token containing any nonce claim, even with an otherwise valid signature/events object. A valid login ID token is not a Logout Token. Retain replay handling and the exact selected sessions. Compare an authentic synthetic logout token with an otherwise valid login ID token and a wrong-session token; UI logout alone proves no refresh-family revocation.
